title: A Comparative Survey: Reusing Small Pre-Trained Models for Efficient Large Model Training
problem: Training large language models incurs significant computational costs due to rapid model size expansion. The challenge is to efficiently grow small pre-trained models into larger models using parameter mapping while reducing total training requirements.
motivation: Reducing computational costs in LLM training addresses a critical bottleneck in developing and deploying increasingly large models.
method: The paper provides a uniform evaluation of multiple state-of-the-art model growth techniques that map parameters from small models to large ones using static functions or learned mappings. It systematically compares individual approaches and analyzes combinations of different techniques to identify synergies and improved efficiency.
key_novelty: Systematic comparative evaluation demonstrating that synergistic combinations of model growth techniques can achieve up to 80% reduction in training cost measured in TFLOPs.
contributions: Comprehensive comparative evaluation of multiple model growth techniques
Analysis of combinations and synergies between different methodologies
Demonstration that efficient combinations reduce training cost by up to 80% in TFLOPs
Uniform evaluation framework for systematic comparison across approaches

metrics.other: up to 80% reduction in training cost (TFLOPs)

primary_theme: Model growth optimization for efficient LLM training
